lede: UltraVena is a tabletop machine that scans a forearm with a motorised ultrasound probe, finds the fistula, and stamps an ink dot where the needle should go. Nothing pierces the skin.
stage: Design stage. CAD version 6 is the current iteration and nothing has been built yet.

stats.l: most the probe can press, by estimate

steps: The user rests a forearm on the padded rest and the lights come on.
Two depth cameras build a 3D surface of the forearm.
The user taps a spot on the touchscreen.
The probe tilts square to the skin and lowers until it feels light contact.
The probe steps along the arm while a model outlines the vessel in each image.
Three independent sensors check the arm has not moved.
Software picks the point from the vessel's depth, width and position.
The probe lifts, shifts, and a small actuator presses an ink tip onto the skin.
status: CAD version 6 is the current iteration, still open to changes
Current picks have listings and prices, part swaps still expected
First full plan written, will change as parts are finalised
Version 2 works on generated images, waiting on real scans
Butterfly confirmed real-time streaming, details to settle

team.intro: UltraVena is the senior design project of Team 7 in Electrical and Systems Engineering at the University of Pennsylvania.
